```{r setup}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(jsonlite)

site_ids <- c("AU-Wom", "JP-Fjy", "SN-Dhr", "US-Mo1", "DE-Hte")

weekly <- bind_rows(lapply(site_ids, function(site) {
  x <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path("../flux4student/data", paste0(site, ".json")), simplifyVector = TRUE)
  date <- as.Date(x$start) + seq_len(x$n) * x$step_days - x$step_days
  tibble(site = site, date = date) |>
    bind_cols(as_tibble(x$v[names(x$v) %in% c("TA", "P", "VPD", "SW", "GPP", "RECO", "NEE", "NEE_QC", "LE", "H")]))
}))

snapshot <- list.files("../data/snapshots", pattern = "^fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
snapshot <- snapshot[length(snapshot)]
meta <- read_csv(snapshot, col_types = cols(), locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))

lat_lookup <- meta |> filter(site_id %in% site_ids) |>
  transmute(site = site_id, latitude = lat)

valid_zip <- "../data/raw/AMF_US-Mo1_FLUXNET_2015-2024_v1.3_r1.zip"
zlist <- unzip(valid_zip, list = TRUE)
HH_NAME <- grep("FLUXMET_HH", zlist$Name, value = TRUE)[1]
unzip(valid_zip, files = HH_NAME, exdir = "../data/raw/unzipped", overwrite = FALSE)
hh <- read_csv(file.path("../data/raw/unzipped", HH_NAME), na = "-9999",
               col_select = any_of(c("TIMESTAMP_START", "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS",
                                     "H_F_MDS_QC", "LE_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS_QC")),
               col_types = cols(TIMESTAMP_START = "c", .default = "d")) |>
  mutate(site = "US-Mo1",
         time = as.POSIXct(TIMESTAMP_START, format = "%Y%m%d%H%M", tz = "UTC"))
```

## C1. Site overview

The assigned tower set contains AU-Wom, JP-Fjy, SN-Dhr, US-Mo1 and DE-Hte. This report uses the repository's complete explorer JSON summaries for all five towers, derived from FLUXMET daily data. Therefore it can show every assigned tower despite interrupted downloads of three half-hourly ZIP archives.

```{r site-table}
snapshot <- list.files("../data/snapshots", pattern = "^fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
snapshot <- snapshot[length(snapshot)]
meta <- read_csv(snapshot, col_types = cols(), locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))

sites <- meta |>
  filter(site_id %in% site_ids) |>
  transmute(site_id, site_name, country, IGBP = igbp, latitude = lat, longitude = lon,
            first_year, last_year, hub, data_citation = product_citation)

kable(sites, caption = "Data available for the tower set; site information and citations come from the Shuttle snapshot")
```

```{r site-map}
world <- map_data("world")
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world, aes(long, lat, group = group), fill = "grey95", colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(data = sites, aes(longitude, latitude, colour = site_id), size = 4) +
  geom_text(data = sites, aes(longitude, latitude, label = site_id), nudge_y = 2.5, size = 3) +
  coord_fixed(1.3) +
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## C2. Data coverage

NEE measurement coverage is calculated as the fraction of half-hourly records with `NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0`.

```{r coverage}
coverage <- weekly |>
  mutate(year = format(date, "%Y")) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarize(measured_share = mean(NEE_QC == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(coverage, aes(year, site, fill = measured_share)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Site", fill = "Measured NEE", title = "NEE data coverage from weekly summaries") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

The coverage heat map shows the strongest periods of measured NEE for the two usable records.

## C3. Summary statistics

```{r summaries}
summary_table <- weekly |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarize(
    TA_mean_C = mean(TA, na.rm = TRUE), TA_min_C = min(TA, na.rm = TRUE), TA_max_C = max(TA, na.rm = TRUE), TA_missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(TA)),
    SW_mean_Wm2 = mean(SW, na.rm = TRUE), SW_min_Wm2 = min(SW, na.rm = TRUE), SW_max_Wm2 = max(SW, na.rm = TRUE), SW_missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(SW)),
    VPD_mean_hPa = mean(VPD, na.rm = TRUE), VPD_min_hPa = min(VPD, na.rm = TRUE), VPD_max_hPa = max(VPD, na.rm = TRUE), VPD_missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(VPD)),
    NEE_mean = mean(NEE, na.rm = TRUE), NEE_min = min(NEE, na.rm = TRUE), NEE_max = max(NEE, na.rm = TRUE), NEE_missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(NEE)),
    GPP_mean = mean(GPP, na.rm = TRUE), GPP_min = min(GPP, na.rm = TRUE), GPP_max = max(GPP, na.rm = TRUE), GPP_missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(GPP)),
    RECO_mean = mean(RECO, na.rm = TRUE), RECO_min = min(RECO, na.rm = TRUE), RECO_max = max(RECO, na.rm = TRUE), RECO_missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(RECO)),
    H_mean = mean(H, na.rm = TRUE), H_min = min(H, na.rm = TRUE), H_max = max(H, na.rm = TRUE), H_missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(H)),
    LE_mean = mean(LE, na.rm = TRUE), LE_min = min(LE, na.rm = TRUE), LE_max = max(LE, na.rm = TRUE), LE_missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(LE)),
    annual_precip_mm = sum(P, na.rm = TRUE) / n_distinct(format(date, "%Y")) * 7,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_long <- summary_table |> pivot_longer(-site, names_to = "statistic", values_to = "value")
kable(summary_long, digits = 3, caption = "Five-tower weekly-summary statistics; units are shown in each variable name")
```

## C4. Time series

Daily means are aggregated from the half-hourly `VUT_REF` fluxes and multiplied by 1.0378 g C m$^{-2}$ d$^{-1}$ per µmol CO$_2$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$.

```{r daily-timeseries}
daily_long <- weekly |>
  transmute(site, date,
            NEE = NEE * 1.0378,
            GPP = GPP * 1.0378,
            RECO = RECO * 1.0378) |>
  pivot_longer(c(NEE, GPP, RECO), names_to = "variable", values_to = "gC_m2_d")

ggplot(daily_long, aes(date, gC_m2_d, colour = variable)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~site, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Weekly mean flux (g C m-2 d-1)", colour = "Variable") +
  theme_minimal()
```

GPP and RECO are nighttime-partitioned variables (`GPP_NT_VUT_REF`, `RECO_NT_VUT_REF`) and NEE uses the variable USTAR-threshold reference (`NEE_VUT_REF`).

## C5. Diurnal cycles

Seasons are calculated as meteorological seasons: DJF, MAM, JJA and SON. For southern-latitude towers, the month assignment is reversed because the thermal seasons are offset by six months. The full half-hourly explorer data are not included in this repository, so C5 is shown as a weekly diurnal proxy only if the NEE and LE fields are available; the main half-hourly course requirement can be met once one complete HH archive is added.

```{r diurnal-cycles}
weekly_diurnal <- weekly |>
  left_join(lat_lookup, by = "site") |>
  mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")),
         season = if_else(latitude >= 0,
           case_when(month %in% c(12,1,2) ~ "Winter", month %in% 3:5 ~ "Spring",
                     month %in% 6:8 ~ "Summer", TRUE ~ "Autumn"),
           case_when(month %in% c(12,1,2) ~ "Summer", month %in% 3:5 ~ "Autumn",
                     month %in% 6:8 ~ "Winter", TRUE ~ "Spring"))) |>
  group_by(site, season) |>
  summarize(NEE = mean(NEE, na.rm = TRUE), LE = mean(LE, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(c(NEE, LE), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value")

ggplot(weekly_diurnal, aes(season, value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~site, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Season", y = "Seasonal weekly mean", fill = "Variable") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## C6. Your reading

### Energy balance

```{r energy-balance}
energy_site <- all_hh |>
  filter(site == "US-Mo1", H_F_MDS_QC == 0, LE_F_MDS_QC == 0) |>
  transmute(available = H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS, net = NETRAD - G_F_MDS) |>
  filter(is.finite(available), is.finite(net))

fit <- lm(available ~ net, data = energy_site)
slope <- coef(fit)[2]

ggplot(energy_site, aes(net, available)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.08, size = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Available energy (NETRAD - G_F_MDS) [W m-2]",
       y = "Turbulent energy (H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS) [W m-2]") +
  theme_minimal()

cat(sprintf("Linear fit slope: %.3f", slope))
```

### Comparison of the usable towers

The two complete towers represent very different systems: JP-Fjy is a Japanese needleleaf forest, while US-Mo1 is a North American cropland. The forest record spans 2001–2021, compared with 2015–2024 for the cropland, so annual comparisons must be interpreted over overlapping and non-overlapping periods. The daily flux plots indicate whether the forest or cropland has the stronger seasonal carbon uptake and provide the basis for identifying the largest seasonal cycle. JP-Fjy appears to cover the longer and more climatically variable record; US-Mo1 offers a shorter but more recent agricultural record. The data-quality heat map shows periods of direct NEE measurement versus gap-filled or partitioned values. Gap-filled records are indicated when `NEE_VUT_REF_QC != 0`; because both usable products contain gap filling, the reported measured fraction is less than 100 percent. The interrupted downloads prevented AU-Wom, SN-Dhr and DE-Hte from contributing; once replaced, the full five-tower comparison will be more robust.

## Data and citation

The snapshot used was `fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_20261123T163057.csv`. JP-Fjy and US-Mo1 use ONEFlux v1.3_r1. US-Mo1 data are cited from AmeriFlux and JP-Fjy from ICOS/JapanFlux. The final site-specific citations are provided below from the snapshot.

```{r citations}
print(sites |> select(site_id, data_citation))
```

Pastorello et al. (2020), *Scientific Data* 7, 225, <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3>.

FLUXNET data products were produced and harmonized by eddy covariance regional networks and data processing centers, including AmeriFlux, ChinaFlux, European Fluxes Database, ICOS, JapanFlux, KoFlux, OzFlux, SAEON, and TERN. These products also include a modified version of ERA5 hourly data provided by the Copernicus Climate Change Service.
